what_it_does: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a technique where a language model, before generating an answer, first searches a large knowledge base (like a company's document library) to retrieve relevant passages and include them as context. The bottleneck is the search step: finding the most relevant passages among millions requires a 'nearest-neighbor search' — comparing a query against every stored item to find the closest matches. This paper measures end-to-end RAG pipelines and finds a counterintuitive result: exact search (checking every document precisely) can actually be faster end-to-end than approximate search (using shortcuts that skip many documents), because exact search returns a smaller, higher-quality set of documents that makes the subsequent language-model generation step cheaper. Based on this finding, the paper proposes hardware and system-level acceleration specifically targeted at making exact nearest-neighbor search fast enough to be practical.
